title: This Shark Hunts in Icy Water With a Body Heated Like a Mammal
subject: salmon shark

scenes.text: Most sharks are cold-blooded. This one hunts in icy Alaskan water and runs hot.
The salmon shark lives in seas as cold as two or three degrees Celsius.
Yet its core body stays roughly eight to sixteen degrees warmer than the water around it.
It's a top predator in the Gulf of Alaska, hunting Pacific salmon, herring and pollock.
Scientists call it partly warm-blooded: it holds on to some of its own body heat.
So in the freezing water, the shark is the warm one.
